_doc: Stream E, M2. More vignettes (same format as m1.json; read both). See data/vignettes/README.md.

vignettes.name: The Collapsed Adit
vignettes.blurb: An old mine entrance fallen in; a trapped miner taps on the rubble. Clear the beetles, shift the beam, free him.
vignettes.lore: Tap. Tap-tap. Tap. Someone behind the rubble has been doing that for a while.

objects.name: Rotten beam
objects.text: You heave the beam aside. A filthy hand waves at you through the gap.

objects.name: Ossie the miner
says: Air! Lovely air! I owe you a pint, and a pickaxe, and possibly my life.
Take my lucky lamp. It never once kept me out of trouble.

vignettes.name: The Giant's Cookfire
vignettes.blurb: A cold firepit the size of a cottage with a cart-sized spit and gnawed ox bones; crag hyenas scavenge. Whoever cooked here is not around. Probably.
vignettes.lore: The ashes are cold. The bones are large. The spoon is larger than you.

objects.name: Scratched on a bone
objects.text: COW. COW. GOAT. MAN? NO, TOO STRINGY.

vignettes.name: The Humming Stones
vignettes.blurb: A ring of standing stones that hums at night; a wisp sleeps at its heart. Touch the centre stone at night for a short blessing.
vignettes.lore: Nine stones, leaning in like old men sharing a secret. Put your hand on one and it is faintly warm.

objects.name: Centre stone
objects.text: The hum climbs through your arm. For a little while, your wounds close faster.

vignettes.name: The Toppled King
vignettes.blurb: A broken statue of a forgotten king face-down in the grass; the hollow crown hides a compartment. Rats live in the plinth.
vignettes.lore: Someone pulled down this king a long time ago and nobody bothered to put him back up. His crown is hollow.

objects.name: Compartment in the crown
objects.hint: The stone crown sounds hollow when you knock on it.

objects.name: Chiselled on the plinth
objects.text: KING OSWIN THE UNREMARKABLE. HE TRIED.

vignettes.name: The Last Wagon
vignettes.blurb: A caravan smashed by something big; one survivor in the last wagon, hounds circling. Hold off the pack, then she gives you the caravan's strongbox key.
vignettes.lore: Three wagons on their sides and one still upright. From inside the upright one, a voice says, very calmly, "Are the dogs still there?"

objects.name: Wenna Coombe, spice trader
says: They came out of the long grass, big as ponies. The others ran. I did not run. I am very slow.
The strongbox is under the second wagon. Take what you like, you have earned it.

vignettes.name: The Drowned Chapel
vignettes.blurb: A chapel standing in a lake to its windowsills; the bell still rings when the wind is right. Serpents in the nave, a reliquary in the bell loft.
vignettes.lore: The water comes up to the windows. When the wind blows, the bell rings, and nobody has pulled its rope in forty years.

objects.name: Hymn book, swollen
objects.text: Verse four has been crossed out and someone has written: STOP SINGING, THEY CAN HEAR YOU.

vignettes.name: The Wishing Stump
vignettes.blurb: A huge hollow stump stuffed with old wishes on scraps of cloth; a spider lives in it and eats them. Leave a coin and pull a wish out.
vignettes.lore: A hollow stump stuffed with knotted rags. Each one has a wish written on it. Something has been eating them.

objects.name: Hollow stump
objects.text: You pull out a rag. It says: "I wish my brother would give back my good hat." You leave a coin anyway.

vignettes.name: The Burned Farmstead
vignettes.blurb: A farm burned in a raid; the family's dog still guards the ashes. Brigands come back for the root cellar. Feed the dog and it follows you to the cache.
vignettes.lore: The house is ash and the barn is ash. A thin grey dog sits in the middle of it all, waiting for somebody.

objects.name: A thin grey dog
says: The dog wags once, then trots off and sits by a patch of scorched boards, looking at you.

vignettes.name: Smugglers' Cove
vignettes.blurb: A tide cave mouth with a rowing boat, barrels of untaxed brandy and a lookout who is mostly asleep.
vignettes.lore: Barrels stacked above the tide line, a rowing boat on the shingle, and a lookout snoring with his mouth open.

objects.name: Tide table, annotated
objects.text: Low water Thursday. Bring the good rope this time, Jory.

vignettes.name: The Wreck of the Patience
vignettes.blurb: A merchant ship broken on the rocks; crabs and gulls picking it over. The captain's log and a waterlogged chest.
vignettes.lore: Half a ship lies on the rocks with her name still on the bow: PATIENCE. She ran out of it.

objects.name: Captain's log
objects.text: Day nine. The lighthouse is dark. I am told it is "on strike". I did not know lighthouses could do that.

vignettes.name: The Dark Lighthouse
vignettes.blurb: A lighthouse whose keeper ran off; light it again with a full oil barrel and ships stop wrecking. Moths swarm the lamp room.
vignettes.lore: The lighthouse is dark. A note on the door says GONE FISHING. It is dated four winters ago.

objects.name: Lamp oil barrel
objects.text: You haul the oil up the stairs and light the lamp. Out on the water, somebody cheers.

objects.name: Keeper's note
objects.text: GONE FISHING. Back soon. Do not touch the lamp, it bites.

vignettes.name: Gallows Crossroads
vignettes.blurb: A crossroads gibbet with an empty cage and a signpost someone has turned to point the wrong way. Owls and a ghostly highwayman's stash.
vignettes.lore: The signpost has been turned round. Every arm points at the gibbet.

objects.name: Crooked signpost
objects.text: You turn the signpost back the right way. It creaks, and something drops out of a hollow arm.

objects.name: Highwayman's stash, under the gibbet
objects.hint: The gibbet's base stone is newer than the rest.

vignettes.name: The Flooded Mill
vignettes.blurb: A watermill whose race has burst and flooded the yard; the wheel still turns. A miller asks you to clear the slimes from the sluice.
vignettes.lore: The mill wheel is still turning, but the millpond is in the yard, the kitchen and most of the bedroom.

objects.name: Miller Hollis
says: Something jammed the sluice and now it's jammed with THEM. Clear it and you can have a sack of flour. Or money. Mostly money.

objects.name: Sluice gate
objects.text: You wrench the sluice open and the water drains with a long gurgle.

vignettes.name: The Angry Hives
vignettes.blurb: Skeps on a hillside where a bear-sized boar got into the honey; flitters swarm. Honey sells well.
vignettes.lore: Straw hives, all knocked over. The air is buzzing and the grass is sticky.

objects.name: Honeycomb
objects.text: You scoop out a slab of honeycomb. A market will pay for it, if the bees let you get that far.

vignettes.name: The Hermit's Hollow
vignettes.blurb: A hermit living in a hollow under a fallen pine, who sells advice nobody wants and hints about a hidden cache in the zone.
vignettes.lore: A door built into the roots of a fallen pine. A sign says NO VISITORS. Under it, smaller: (well, maybe one).

objects.name: Brother Emrys, hermit
says: Advice is a copper. Good advice is two. The truth is free, and nobody ever wants it.
There is a box under the third stone from the old well, in the next valley. I put it there. I forget why.

vignettes.name: The Toadstool Ring
vignettes.blurb: A ring of huge mushrooms where sporecaps dance at dusk; step in and you are briefly very small (and fast). Harmless, mostly.
vignettes.lore: A perfect ring of toadstools, each one up to your knee. The grass inside is greener than it has any right to be.

objects.name: Step into the ring
objects.text: The world spins. For a few minutes you feel light on your feet and smell of mushrooms.

vignettes.name: The Abandoned Watchtower
vignettes.blurb: A frontier watchtower left to rot; archers have moved into the top, the signal brazier is unlit. Light it for the garrison.
vignettes.lore: The watch has gone home. The archers in the tower are definitely not the watch.

objects.name: Signal brazier
objects.text: The brazier catches. Far off, another one answers it.

vignettes.name: The Abandoned Siege Camp
vignettes.blurb: A besieger's camp packed up in a hurry; a forgotten ram, cold fires, and hyenas in the latrine trench. Some loot left behind.
vignettes.lore: They left in a hurry. The battering ram is still here, along with a lot of opinions carved into it.

objects.name: Carved on the ram
objects.text: KICK HARDER — Sergeant. WE ARE KICKING — Everybody.

vignettes.name: The Bone Pit
vignettes.blurb: A plague pit at a field edge where the dead have started crawling out; a wandering priest asks you to put them down and say the words.
vignettes.lore: A long hollow in the ground, grassed over, too regular to be natural. The grass is moving.

objects.name: Father Tobin
says: They will not lie still. I have asked nicely. Would you ask less nicely?

objects.name: Grave marker
objects.text: You say the words Father Tobin taught you. The ground goes quiet.

vignettes.name: The Sky Altar
vignettes.blurb: A hilltop altar where sky cultists try to call down a storm; interrupt their chant (kill the zealot) before lightning hits.
vignettes.lore: A ring of robed people on the hilltop, chanting at a cloud. The cloud seems to be listening.

objects.name: Chant sheet
objects.text: Line three: AND THEN THE SKY OPENS. (Bring an umbrella this time.)

vignettes.name: The Quarry Ledge
vignettes.blurb: A half-cut quarry with a crane, blocks left mid-cut and a shale construct still following its last order: guard the stone.
vignettes.lore: Blocks of stone cut and left in neat rows. Something stony is walking up and down them, very seriously.

objects.name: Work order
objects.text: Guard the stone. Do not let anyone take the stone. — Foreman (do NOT ask the golem to fetch tea again)

vignettes.name: The Runaway Cart
vignettes.blurb: An ore cart that jumped its rails and spilled copper down a slope; beetles are eating the ore. Gather the nuggets.
vignettes.lore: A cart lies upside down at the bottom of the slope, and a glittering trail of copper ore leads back up to the rails.

objects.name: Copper nuggets
objects.text: You fill your pockets with copper. Somebody will pay for this. Probably the person whose cart it was.

vignettes.name: The Miners' Lamp Shrine
vignettes.blurb: A niche in the rock full of burnt-out miners' lamps, one for every miner who did not come back. Light one for a blessing.
vignettes.lore: Dozens of little lamps in a niche in the rock. One is still lit. Nobody seems to know who keeps lighting it.

objects.name: Unlit lamp
objects.text: You light a lamp and set it among the others. The rock feels a little less heavy.

vignettes.name: The Frozen Tarn
vignettes.blurb: A mountain pool that never thaws; a frost stalker sleeps on the ice and something glints under it.
vignettes.lore: A small lake frozen solid, even in summer. Under the ice, something gold catches the light.

objects.name: Thin ice
objects.text: You crack the ice with your heel and fish out a cold, heavy coin purse.

vignettes.name: The Avalanche Shelter
vignettes.blurb: A stone hut on the pass road with emergency supplies and a logbook of travellers' complaints; hyenas know people get stuck here.
vignettes.lore: A squat stone hut with a sign: SHELTER — IN CASE OF SNOW, OR WOLVES, OR BOTH.

objects.name: Travellers' logbook
objects.text: Snowed in three days. Ate the soap. Would not recommend. — G.

vignettes.name: The Toll Bridge
vignettes.blurb: A narrow bridge with a toll booth manned by brigands pretending to be the reeve's men; their "official" badges are painted wood.
vignettes.lore: A wooden toll booth with a hand-painted sign: OFFISHUL TOLL. PAY HERE. NO ARGUING.

objects.name: Painted wooden badge
objects.text: OFFISHUL REEVE MAN. Number 1. (There is only one badge.)

vignettes.name: The Empty Stilt House
vignettes.blurb: A fisher's house on stilts over the water, abandoned with dinner still on the table; croakers in the reeds below. A diary explains.
vignettes.lore: A house on stilts above the reeds. The door is open, the table is set, and the soup is very, very old.

objects.name: Fisher's diary
objects.text: The big frog is back. It ate the boat. I am going to my sister's. I am not coming back until it eats something else.

vignettes.name: The Eel Weir
vignettes.blurb: A line of wicker eel traps across a stream; something has been raiding them and the fisher wants it gone. A serpent, it turns out.
vignettes.lore: A row of wicker traps across the stream. Every single one has been bitten open from the outside.

objects.name: Nell Pike, eel-catcher
says: Something long and green has been eating my eels. I want it dead, and I want my eels back, and one of those is going to happen.

vignettes.name: The Stranded Ferry
vignettes.blurb: A ferry pulled up on the bank with a broken rope; the ferryman offers a free crossing if you fetch new rope from bandits who stole it.
vignettes.lore: A flat ferry beached on the mud, its rope cut clean through. The ferryman is sitting on it looking at the sky.

objects.name: Old Gaffer Wat, ferryman
says: Somebody cut my rope and took it. Who steals a rope? Rope thieves, that's who.
The ones with the rope went thataway. Fetch it and you ride free for life. Or a week.

vignettes.name: Heron Island
vignettes.blurb: A reed island reached by stepping stones, with a heron rookery and a lost fishing tackle box; wisps over the water at dusk.
vignettes.lore: A little island of reeds, full of herons who stare at you like you owe them money.

objects.name: Scratched on a stone
objects.text: THE HERONS KNOW WHAT YOU DID.

vignettes.name: The Market Cross
vignettes.blurb: A stone market cross where a travelling pedlar sets up; he buys junk and sells rumours. Cutpurses work the crowd.
vignettes.lore: A worn stone cross where the road meets the lane. A pedlar has spread a blanket at its foot covered in things nobody needs.

objects.name: Cadoc the pedlar
says: Rumours! Spoons! Rumours about spoons! Something for everyone.
They say a brigand in the hills buried his takings under a dolmen. They say a lot of things, mind.

vignettes.name: The Rattling Grate
vignettes.blurb: A sewer outfall below a city wall, its grate rattling; rats pour out, and a city clerk's lost ledger is tangled in the bars.
vignettes.lore: A barred outfall at the foot of the wall. The grate rattles. The grate is not being rattled by the wind.

objects.name: Soggy city ledger
objects.text: Item: one (1) sewer grate, repairs to. Approved. Item: sewer grate repairs, cancelled. Reason: rats.

vignettes.name: The Shut-Up Inn
vignettes.blurb: A roadside inn boarded up after a "small fire"; the cellar still holds barrels, and the old landlord's ghost is a carrion moth swarm. Not really a ghost.
vignettes.lore: A boarded-up inn with a sign of a smiling pig. The windows are scorched. Somebody has written CLOSED on the door, then crossed it out and written REALLY CLOSED.

objects.name: Landlord's notice
objects.text: Small fire. Nobody hurt. Pig fine. Re-opening soon. (Not soon.)

vignettes.name: The Lord's Folly
vignettes.blurb: A fake ruin built by a bored noble as a garden ornament, now really ruined; a statue of the noble with a pompous plaque and a hidden wine cellar.
vignettes.lore: A fake ancient ruin, built twenty years ago by a lord who wanted one. Now it really is a ruin. He would be thrilled.

objects.name: Brass plaque
objects.text: THIS ANCIENT RUIN WAS BUILT BY LORD GARRICK MILLWARD. IT IS VERY OLD (FROM NOW ON).

objects.name: His lordship's wine cellar
objects.hint: One column is hollow and has a keyhole.

vignettes.name: The Grey Orchard
vignettes.blurb: An apple orchard turned grey by the blight; the apples are hard as stones and the sporecaps have moved in. One tree still bears a red apple.
vignettes.lore: Every tree is grey, every leaf is grey, every apple is grey. Except one. One red apple, right at the top.

objects.name: The last red apple
objects.text: You pick the apple. It is warm, and crisp, and for a moment the whole orchard looks green again.

vignettes.name: The Warband Totem
vignettes.blurb: A totem of skulls marking warband ground; smash it and the war grip weakens (later); for now a cache of plunder and a few imps.
vignettes.lore: A pole of skulls and rags, and a lot of scratches on the ground that look like a map of where they plan to burn next.

objects.name: Skull totem
objects.text: You topple the totem. The skulls roll off down the hill, and somewhere a warband will be very cross.

vignettes.name: The Smoking Crater
vignettes.blurb: A crater still smoking from something that fell; ash wisps dance in it and a hot, strange stone lies at the bottom.
vignettes.lore: A fresh crater, the grass around it scorched in a perfect circle. At the bottom, something glows like a coal.

objects.name: Farmer's complaint
objects.text: To the Reeve: a STAR has landed in my barley. Please send someone to remove it. Also my barley.

vignettes.name: The Chained Oak
vignettes.blurb: A great oak bound in iron chains by a long-dead order; something under its roots still scratches. Break the chains at your own risk (a rift horror? no, just hounds, phew).
vignettes.lore: An old oak wrapped in rusted chains, padlocked, nailed. Someone really did not want this tree going anywhere.

objects.name: Rusted padlock
objects.text: The padlock falls apart in your hand. The roots go still. Nothing comes out. Probably good?

objects.name: Stone inscription
objects.text: BOUND BY THE ORDER OF THE LANTERN. DO NOT UNBIND. DO NOT EVEN ASK.

vignettes.name: The Pilgrims' Rest
vignettes.blurb: A pilgrim camp at a roadside shrine; pilgrims beg an escort past wolves on the next stretch and trade relic charms.
vignettes.lore: Tents, a cook-pot, a lot of sore feet. A dozen pilgrims look up at you with great hope and greater blisters.

objects.name: Sister Edda
says: Bless you for stopping. The hounds follow us like we were sausages.
Take a pilgrim's charm. It won't help, but it's very nicely carved.

vignettes.name: The Wayside Saint
vignettes.blurb: A tiny roadside shrine to Saint Orrin with a donation box someone has been robbing; catch the thief (a rat, very large).
vignettes.lore: A little roof over a little statue of a saint with one hand raised. The donation box has been gnawed open.

objects.name: Donation box
objects.text: You leave a coin and straighten the saint's hat. You feel watched over, a bit.

vignettes.name: The Fallen Bell
vignettes.blurb: A monastery bell tower collapsed, the great bell cracked on the ground; owls nest in it. Ring it once for a blessing and a swarm.
vignettes.lore: The bell lies on its side in the grass, cracked down the middle. Owls have nested inside it, which seems fair.

objects.name: Cracked bell
objects.text: BONNNG. The owls are furious. You feel oddly blessed.

vignettes.name: The Old Battlefield
vignettes.blurb: A field of rusted armour and a broken standard from a battle whose reason is long forgotten; barrow hounds hunt the bones.
vignettes.lore: Rusty helmets in the grass, a snapped spear every few paces. Nobody can say who won. Possibly nobody did.

objects.name: Torn standard
objects.text: Someone has embroidered on it: WE WERE RIGHT. Someone else has added underneath: NO.

vignettes.name: The Stair to Nowhere
vignettes.blurb: A grand stone stair rising out of the ground and ending in mid-air; at the top, a chest; at the bottom, a mimic pretending to be another chest.
vignettes.lore: A great stone staircase climbs out of the grass, twenty steps up, and stops. At the top, a chest. At the bottom, another chest. Hm.

objects.name: Faded warning
objects.text: Only one of them is a chest.

vignettes.name: The Reed Hide
vignettes.blurb: A hunter's hide in the reeds with a dead hunter, his bow and his last tally of a beast he never got; finish the count.
vignettes.lore: A neat little hide woven from reeds. Inside, a tally on a board: forty-one marks, and the word BIG next to the last.

objects.name: Tally board
objects.text: 41. BIG. Still out there. Will get it tomorrow.

vignettes.name: The Peat Cutters' Camp
vignettes.blurb: Peat cutters' camp with stacked turves drying; bog slimes have come up through the cuttings. Buy fuel, or take it.
vignettes.lore: Neat stacks of dark peat drying in the wind, and a hole in the bog where somebody dug too deep.

objects.name: Orla the cutter
says: Dug a bit too deep, didn't we. Now the bog's digging back.

vignettes.name: The Lantern Path
vignettes.blurb: A path of floating lights across the fen that leads walkers astray; follow them backwards to a drowned traveller's purse.
vignettes.lore: Little lights bob over the fen in a neat row, like lanterns on a path. There is no path.

objects.name: Waterlogged map
objects.text: Follow the lights. They know the way. (They did not.)

vignettes.name: The Charcoal Burners
vignettes.blurb: Smoking charcoal clamps in a clearing; the burners have gone, leaving one clamp about to flare. Wolves circle.
vignettes.lore: Mounds of earth smoke quietly in the clearing. One of them is smoking rather more loudly than the others.

objects.name: Flaring clamp
objects.text: You shovel earth over the flaring clamp until it settles back to a sulky smoke.

vignettes.name: The Axe in the Stump
vignettes.blurb: A splendid axe stuck in a stump that nobody can pull out; a sign offers a prize to whoever can. You can, after the boar is dealt with.
vignettes.lore: A beautiful axe, buried head-deep in a stump. A sign: WHOEVER PULLS OUT THIS AXE MAY KEEP IT. (Please, somebody.)

vignettes.name: The Stag Shrine
vignettes.blurb: A forest clearing with a stag's skull on a post and offerings of acorns; the old forest folk still come. A dread stag? No, just deer bones and owls.
vignettes.lore: A great stag skull on a pole, antlers hung with ribbons and acorns. The clearing is very quiet.

objects.name: Leave an acorn
objects.text: You leave an acorn. The wind moves through the trees like someone saying thank you.

vignettes.name: The Trapper's Line
vignettes.blurb: A line of snares and a trapper's cache; one snare holds something too big for it (a hyena, very cross).
vignettes.lore: Snares strung between trees, and one of them has caught something that does not fit in it at all.

objects.name: Trapper's rules
objects.text: 1. Check the snares. 2. If something big is in the snare, leave it there. 3. Leave.

vignettes.name: The Moonlight Stones
vignettes.blurb: Flat stones on a hilltop where pedlars of uncertain origin trade at night; by day only scattered trinkets and a moth swarm.
vignettes.lore: Flat stones in a ring, scattered with odd things: a glass eye, half a key, a very small boot.

objects.name: Price list on a slate
objects.text: One wish: three sneezes. One secret: a good one back. One boot: just the one boot.
